citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be essentially small abelian categories and let
$\mathcal D,\mathcal D'$ be essentially small additive categories. For any
abelian group $H$, every function
$\chi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)\to H$ satisfying
$\chi(Y)=\chi(X)+\chi(Z)$ for every short exact sequence
$0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\chi\colon G_0(\mathcal C)\to H$ with
$\overline\chi([X])=\chi(X)$. Every function
$\psi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)\to H$ satisfying
$\psi(X\oplus Y)=\psi(X)+\psi(Y)$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\psi\colon K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathcal D)\to H$ with
$\overline\psi([X])=\psi(X)$. Here $\operatorname{Iso}$ is the set of
isomorphism classes, so these are class functions.

An exact functor between essentially small abelian categories induces a
homomorphism on $G_0$, and an additive functor between essentially small
additive categories induces a homomorphism on split $K_0$. These assignments
preserve identities and composition. Naturally isomorphic exact functors, or
naturally isomorphic additive functors, induce equal homomorphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $K(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(K(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(K(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]].

**The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]].

**The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

**The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$.

**The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a generalized-standard composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):K(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):K(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i).

**Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is generated by the ground vector $D_{A_\Lambda}$ over $\mathbb Q$ and is identified with the form-dual family by the same theorem. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices.

**Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ on $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]] are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2], and they intertwine with the category-O residue functors through the Schur quotient: $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$, compatibly with residue projectors and dualities, by [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]]. On the category-O side the induced $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley operators, and a residue translate of a simple either vanishes along an absent crystal edge or is a self-dual indecomposable whose simple head and socle is the translated label, by [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]]; ungraded at parameter $1$ these are exactly the operators $e_i,f_i$ on the Fock module, so under $\Phi$ the residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators, giving the first half of (ii).

**Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with no further costandard vectors, standard lattice or residue operators. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v).

**Crystal reachability.** By step 3.1 a residue translate of a simple is zero or a self-dual indecomposable with simple head and socle the crystal-translated label, and the residue operators are the Fock Chevalley operators; starting from the ground simple $D(A_\Lambda)$ and following any reduced crystal word to $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, each intermediate translate is nonzero (the corresponding crystal edge exists along the word) and exactness of the residue functors makes the final simple a composition factor of the word applied to the ground. Conversely, a simple composition factor of any residue word applied to the ground lies in the highest crystal component, which is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ because the highest weight Fock module is generated by the ground monomial and its standard monomials are indexed by $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ ([[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]). This proves (iv).

**Rational ground cyclicity.** Over $\mathbb Q$ the element $D_{A_\Lambda}$ is a highest weight vector for the integrable action of step 3.1, and $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$ is irreducible: it is the dual of the irreducible highest weight module, and the span over $\mathbb Q$ of the orbit of the ground vector is a nonzero submodule, hence all of $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$. Thus the ground class generates $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, proving the rational clause of (iii).

**The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$ and the costandard basis $(D_{00},D_{01},D_{11})$ of the three nonzero content classes. The residue operators act by $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$, $fD_{11}=0$ and $eD_{00}=0$, $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$; this is the degree-one block $B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ sitting in degree two as a corner together with the two-dimensional block $M_2(\mathbb C)$, where $D_{11}$ is two-dimensional with $x\mapsto0$ on the simple and the second divided power $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$, $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. The lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}:=\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ contains the ground, is stable under $f,e$ and their divided powers and under the toral operators, and does not contain $D_{01}$: any element whose $D_{01}$-coordinate is odd lies outside, and the operators multiply $D_{01}$-coefficients by even integers. Hence $L_{\mathbb Z}$ is a proper integral costandard submodule containing the ground vector, so the costandard lattice is not ground cyclic over $\mathbb Z$ even under divided powers, while dividing by $2$ over $\mathbb Q$ restores cyclicity; this proves the failure clause of (iii) and, with step 5.1, the first half of (v).

**Conclusion.** Step 2.1 identifies $G_0$ with the full integral costandard lattice and step 2.2 computes the Specht classes, proving (i); step 2.3 gives the divided-power integral forms and step 3.1 identifies the residue operators with the Chevalley operators, proving (ii); step 5.1 proves rational ground cyclicity, step 2.3 proves integral ground generation of the standard lattice and step 6.1 exhibits the index-two failure of integral costandard cyclicity, proving (iii) and its sharpness; step 4.1 proves the crystal reachability statement (iv); and step 3.2 (level zero) together with steps 5.1 and 6.1 separates the rational-cyclicity and categorical reachability conclusions from integral costandard cyclicity, as asserted in (v). No step identifies $\{D_A\}$ with the standard divided-power lattice, and no integral costandard generation is used.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Fix a nonempty set $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ of consecutive integers (possibly all of
$\mathbb Z$ or half-infinite), put $I^+:=I\cup(I+1)$, fix a level $l\ge1$ and an
integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, and let
$\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^{l}\Lambda_{m_j}\in P^+$ be the corresponding dominant
integral weight. Throughout, the ground field is $\mathbb C$ and the degree-$d$
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra $H_d(m)$ is the algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: the quotient of the degenerate
affine Hecke algebra by the relation $(x_1-m_1)\cdots(x_1-m_l)=0$, with
$\mathbb C$-basis $\{x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w\}$ over $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$,
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}H_d(m)=l^d d!$. The $x_1,\dots,x_d$ commute pairwise.

**(1) Joint spectral idempotents and content idempotents.** For
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in\mathbb Z^d$ let $e(i)\in H_d(m)$ be the joint polynomial
spectral idempotent of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ that projects onto the generalized joint
eigenspace with generalized eigenvalues $i_1,\dots,i_d$; these idempotents are
those of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
they lie in the commutative subalgebra generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$, are
mutually orthogonal, sum to the identity of $H_d(m)$, and all but finitely many
are zero. For $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $d=\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$ put

$$I_\alpha:=\{\,i\in I^d\ :\ \textstyle\sum_{r=1}^{d}\alpha_{i_r}=\alpha\,\},\qquad e_\alpha:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}e(i)\in H_d(m),\qquad H^\Lambda_\alpha:=e_\alpha H_d(m).$$

Because $I_\alpha$ is finite (so only finitely many nonzero $e(i)$ occur in it),
$e_\alpha$ is an idempotent of $H_d(m)$, nonzero or zero, and $H^\Lambda_\alpha$
is a finite-dimensional algebra with identity $e_\alpha$. Its (finite
dimensional, unital) left modules are exactly the $H_d(m)$-modules on which
$e_\alpha$ acts as the identity.

**(2) The supported degree and the tower.** The **degree-$d$ supported tower
algebra** is $f_{I,d}H_d(m)$ with $f_{I,d}:=\sum_{i\in I^d}e(i)$; for
$I\ne\mathbb Z$ this is in general a proper central cut of the whole degree-$d$
algebra $H_d(m)$, and no equality with $H_d(m)$ is asserted. The **tower** is

$$H^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha .$$

It is a unital algebra when $I$ is finite and a locally unital algebra in
general; the ambient tower inclusion is the degree-raising embedding
$\iota\colon H_d(m)\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}(m)$ of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
At level $0$ the tower is concentrated in degree $0$: $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$
and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$.

**(3) Grothendieck groups and the Cartan pairing.** For each $\alpha$ let
$D(A)$ range over representatives of the simple finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules and $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ over their
projective covers. The **module Grothendieck group** $G_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is
the Grothendieck group $G_0$ of the category of finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]])
and the **split projective group** $K_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]); both are taken block
by block and then summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. The **Cartan pairing**

$$\langle-,-\rangle\colon K_0(H^\Lambda)\times G_0(H^\Lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \langle[P],[M]\rangle:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{H^\Lambda}(P,M),$$

is the object-level Hom pairing of
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]; its biadditivity
on the two groups is the descent proved in
[[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]], which also shows
that $\{[Y(A)]\}$ and $\{[D(A)]\}$ are dual bases (over $\mathbb C$ every simple
endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$). Different blocks are orthogonal.

**(4) Residue maps and residue functors.** For $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q^+$
the embedding $\iota$ composed with the projection onto the block
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is the non-unital algebra homomorphism

$$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad u_{\alpha,i}:=\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}(e_\alpha)=\sum_{i\in I_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\ i_{d+1}=i}e(i).$$

The **residue restriction functor** $e_i$ sends a finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$-module $M$ to the vector space
$u_{\alpha,i}M$ viewed as an $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module through
$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$, and the **residue induction functor** $f_i$ sends a
finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module $M$ to
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}M$. Their
well-definedness, exactness, biadjointness, compatibility with the duality
$\circledast$ of (5), and their effect on Grothendieck groups (adjoint operators
for the Cartan pairing, by
[[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]]) are the
content of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]];
summing over $\alpha$ gives endofunctors $e_i,f_i$ of the tower.

**(5) Duality.** The anti-automorphism $\ast$ of $H_d(m)$ with
$s_r^\ast=s_r$ and $x_r^\ast=x_r$ preserves each $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. On
finite-dimensional left $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules put
$M^{\circledast}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(M,\mathbb C)$ with left action
$(hf)(m):=f(m)h^\ast$. This duality fixes every simple module and commutes with
the residue functors; it is the ordinary duality recorded in
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]],
and it is used throughout this page in the form $M^{\circledast}$.

**(6) Stable and admissible data.** A charge datum as above is used in the
form of its admissible stable realization of
[[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]];
stable range means at least $d$ Jordan strings of maximal length $l$, and
admissibility means $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$ for the origin $c$.
These hypotheses are only invoked where the corresponding supplier is used;
the definitions (1)-(5) themselves do not assume them.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in the dominance order of [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] for every
$j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ with column reading $a_1,\dots,a_n$ (read column by column,
bottom to top, [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]) put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Keep the pyramid and admissible origins $c$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], the
ground object $P_c$, the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ and its
central decomposition. For a charge $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d$
let $I_\alpha$ be the finite set of residue sequences of content $\alpha$, and
let $T_\alpha$ be the corresponding central component of $T$; in the integral
model
$$T_\alpha=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}P_c,$$
the sum of the residue-induction images of the ground object. Put
$$B_\alpha:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the corresponding central component of the Hecke image algebra (the opposite
convention is fixed here), and define the **Schur functor** of the block by
$$\pi_\alpha:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha,-)\colon\mathcal O_\alpha^d\to B_\alpha\text{-mod}.$$
Its left adjoint is $\pi^*_\alpha:=T_\alpha\otimes_{B_\alpha}-$.

The verification below records the properties used on this page and marks the
boundaries explicitly: $\pi_\alpha$ is exact, being Hom from a projective
object; its left adjoint is right exact but not exact in general; it sends
$B_\alpha$-projectives to projective objects and $\pi^*_\alpha\pi_\alpha$
recovers $\operatorname{add}(T_\alpha)$, including every standard-labelled
prinjective; neither exactness of $\pi^*_\alpha$ nor recovery of every
category-$\mathcal O$ projective is asserted, both failing in the two-equal-charge
rank-one example of the companion page. The components assemble as a locally
unital sum over the charges, and all ambient labels, including those killed by
$\pi$, remain in the category $\mathcal O$.

consumed_sections.Statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$; let
$f_i^{\mathcal O},e_i^{\mathcal O}$ be the residue translation functors on the
sum of parabolic blocks of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] and let
$f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ be the Hecke residue functors of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
Then there are natural isomorphisms
$$f_i^{H}\pi\cong\pi f_i^{\mathcal O},\qquad e_i^{H}\pi\cong\pi e_i^{\mathcal O},$$
where $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ is the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
compatible with the residue eigenvalue projectors, the units and counits of the
two adjunctions, and with ordinary restricted duality and the $*$-duality of the
Hecke side. Consequently the ungraded Grothendieck operators at parameter $1$
agree and the Schur quotient is a module map over the Hecke algebra. For
admissible nonintegral origins the category $\mathcal O$ side uses the genuine
typed coset realization, not an unqualified integer block. The statement
preserves the actual residue and standard filtrations; no graded parity or
Koszul lift is asserted by these ungraded suppliers.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be essentially small abelian categories and let
$\mathcal D,\mathcal D'$ be essentially small additive categories. For any
abelian group $H$, every function
$\chi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)\to H$ satisfying
$\chi(Y)=\chi(X)+\chi(Z)$ for every short exact sequence
$0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\chi\colon G_0(\mathcal C)\to H$ with
$\overline\chi([X])=\chi(X)$. Every function
$\psi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)\to H$ satisfying
$\psi(X\oplus Y)=\psi(X)+\psi(Y)$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\psi\colon K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathcal D)\to H$ with
$\overline\psi([X])=\psi(X)$. Here $\operatorname{Iso}$ is the set of
isomorphism classes, so these are class functions.

An exact functor between essentially small abelian categories induces a
homomorphism on $G_0$, and an additive functor between essentially small
additive categories induces a homomorphism on split $K_0$. These assignments
preserve identities and composition. Naturally isomorphic exact functors, or
naturally isomorphic additive functors, induce equal homomorphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, a degree $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space with its finite W-algebra image
$W_d$ and cyclotomic Hecke image $B_d$. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$; this is the raw double centralizer.
2. For admissible origins, $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence between
   $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.
3. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact
   Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully
   faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all
   tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers
   $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but not every projective.
4. In the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the algebra $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic
   algebra $H_d(\mathbf a)$; outside the stable range and for admissible
   origins the central-corner identification $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ is used.

Mutual centralizers alone do not give the Morita statement: the nonadmissible
origin example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$ and $d=2$ has a nonprojective tensor
module while the mutual centralizer identities still hold.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The exact residue
functors of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] on the
genuine finite-$n$ parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free
generalized-standard flags given by the valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

(1) Their $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock
Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the
standard basis.

(2) For each simple $L(A)$, a residue translate vanishes exactly when the
corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual
indecomposable with simple equal head and socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$, respectively
$L(\tilde e_iA)$.

(3) The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the
ground-state class, with
$M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one
highest constituent.

No action on labels alone proves the $K_0$ relations or the head/socle
statement.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, and let $N(A),K(A)$ denote the standard and
costandard objects of the relevant parabolic summand, $L(A)$ the simples and
$P(A)$ the projective covers, indexed by admissible labels $A$; let
$\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d(\mathbf a)\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(K(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(K(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):K(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the genuine tableau
$K_0$/Fock identification at $s=1$
([[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]). For
every label $A$,
$$[L(A)]=L_A,\qquad [P(A)]=P_A,\qquad [T(A)]=T_A .$$
The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG reciprocity; the tilting
coefficients are the **opposite/reverse-column** composition coefficients
$\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not
generally the inverse-transpose of the original composition matrix. Simples,
projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and
canonical Fock families respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no
Koszul grading and no identification of the library upper and lower families is
asserted.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital algebra over a field $k$. Write
$S_1,\ldots,S_t$ for representatives of the isomorphism classes of simple
left $A$-modules, and choose a finite-dimensional projective cover
$q_i\colon P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ for each $i$. Then the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective left $A$-modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]) is the free abelian
group with basis $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$. In particular, each selected cover is
indecomposable, the $P_i$ are pairwise nonisomorphic, and every finite
dimensional projective is a finite direct sum of them. This result makes no
claim that the Cartan map to the short-exact-sequence group $G_0(A)$ is
invertible.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative $k$-algebra. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent all isomorphism classes of simple left $A$-modules, and let $q_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite-dimensional projective covers. Then $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$ and $[S_1],\ldots,[S_t]$ are bases of $K_0(A)$ and $G_0(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_A=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_A(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ In particular, if $\operatorname{End}_A(S_i)=k$ for every $i$, these bases are dual.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra, let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent the graded-simple shift orbits and let $p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite graded projective covers. Here graded-simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero graded submodule. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. Neither pairing statement asserts unimodularity of the projective-to-module Cartan map or of a projective/projective Cartan matrix. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebra. For a
finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and finite-dimensional left
$A$-module $M$, define the object-level value

$$h(P,M):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,M).$$

If $A$ is $\mathbb Z$-graded and $P,M$ are finite-dimensional graded left $A$-modules,
with $P$ projective in the degree-zero graded category, define

$$h_{\mathrm{gr}}(P,M):=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}v^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M),$$

where $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M)$ consists of $A$-linear maps sending each
$P_i$ into $M_{i+d}$. These are candidate values on object isomorphism
classes; no descent to pairings on $K_0\times G_0$ is asserted here.

$k$-algebras. Write $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$ and
$B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$ for their categories of finite-dimensional
left modules. Let
$F:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$

derivations.claim: **The split $K_0$ basis of covers.** Every simple finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-module has a projective cover, unique up to isomorphism, and the classes $[Y(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, of the covers of the simples $D(A)$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the split Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules; this is [F1] applied block by block and summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$.

**The left adjoint on projectives.** The Schur quotient $\pi$ has a left adjoint $\pi^*$ which is right exact on all modules and sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $\pi^*(Y(A))=P(A)$ and $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so $\pi^*$ recovers the standard-labelled prinjectives, and its exactness on arbitrary modules is not needed. These are the statements of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]].

**The standard lattice and its ground generation.** The standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ has $\mathbb Z$-basis $\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$, the source vector $P_A$ lies in the highest constituent with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}P_A=P_A$, and at parameter one $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)$, so $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ is integrally generated by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators; this is the parameter-one specialization of [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the basis statements of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]].

**The identification $K_0\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$.** Define $\Psi$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Psi([Y(A)])=P_A$; by step 1.3 both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules on the same index set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, so $\Psi$ is a group isomorphism onto $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, giving (i). The identification is realized functorially by $\pi^*$: step 1.2 shows that on projective classes the composite of $\pi^*$ with the category-O identification $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ at parameter one (the projective half of the tableau $K_0$/Fock identification of [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], proved in [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]) is $\Psi$, so no exactness of $\pi^*$ on non-projectives is used.

**The inclusion is the lattice inclusion.** The embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules induces a map on Grothendieck groups; in the category of finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-modules a projective class $[Y(A)]$ maps to the class of the same module, which under the identification $\Phi$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] is the costandard coordinate vector of the module $Y(A)$. By step 1.2, $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so this vector equals the image of $[P(A)]$ under the exact quotient, namely $P_A$ by step 1.3. Hence the composite $\Phi\circ(\text{inclusion})\circ\Psi^{-1}$ is the identity on the basis $\{P_A\}$, i.e. the natural inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$. It is injective because the two bases are distinct integral bases and $\Psi$ is an isomorphism; the pairing-theoretic proof of injectivity via the nondegenerate Shapovalov form on finite weight spaces is the one used in [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]. This proves (ii).

**The Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing.** By [F2] the Cartan pairing descends to $K_0\times G_0$ and pairs the two bases dually; under the identifications of step 2.1 and of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the value on basis vectors is computed on the Fock side, where the pairing between the standard and costandard families at parameter one is the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ with $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ by [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. **Chevalley operators on $K_0$.** The residue functors preserve finite-dimensional projectives: induction across a block is tensoring with the projective left module $H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}$ and restriction is applying the idempotent $u_{\alpha,i}$, both exact and sending projectives to projectives; hence they induce operators on $K_0$, and by [F3] these operators are adjoint to the $G_0$ operators, which are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]. Since $e_i$ and $f_i$ are adjoint to one another under the pairing $C_0$ of step 3.2, the $K_0$ operators are the Chevalley operators as well, proving (iv); the same adjunction is the block-wise adjointness of the residue operators recorded in [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]].

Fix a nonempty set $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ of consecutive integers (possibly all of
$\mathbb Z$ or half-infinite), put $I^+:=I\cup(I+1)$, fix a level $l\ge1$ and an
integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, and let
$\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^{l}\Lambda_{m_j}\in P^+$ be the corresponding dominant
integral weight. Throughout, the ground field is $\mathbb C$ and the degree-$d$
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra $H_d(m)$ is the algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: the quotient of the degenerate
affine Hecke algebra by the relation $(x_1-m_1)\cdots(x_1-m_l)=0$, with
$\mathbb C$-basis $\{x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w\}$ over $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$,
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}H_d(m)=l^d d!$. The $x_1,\dots,x_d$ commute pairwise.

**(1) Joint spectral idempotents and content idempotents.** For
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in\mathbb Z^d$ let $e(i)\in H_d(m)$ be the joint polynomial
spectral idempotent of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ that projects onto the generalized joint
eigenspace with generalized eigenvalues $i_1,\dots,i_d$; these idempotents are
those of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
they lie in the commutative subalgebra generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$, are
mutually orthogonal, sum to the identity of $H_d(m)$, and all but finitely many
are zero. For $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $d=\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$ put

$$I_\alpha:=\{\,i\in I^d\ :\ \textstyle\sum_{r=1}^{d}\alpha_{i_r}=\alpha\,\},\qquad e_\alpha:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}e(i)\in H_d(m),\qquad H^\Lambda_\alpha:=e_\alpha H_d(m).$$

Because $I_\alpha$ is finite (so only finitely many nonzero $e(i)$ occur in it),
$e_\alpha$ is an idempotent of $H_d(m)$, nonzero or zero, and $H^\Lambda_\alpha$
is a finite-dimensional algebra with identity $e_\alpha$. Its (finite
dimensional, unital) left modules are exactly the $H_d(m)$-modules on which
$e_\alpha$ acts as the identity.

**(2) The supported degree and the tower.** The **degree-$d$ supported tower
algebra** is $f_{I,d}H_d(m)$ with $f_{I,d}:=\sum_{i\in I^d}e(i)$; for
$I\ne\mathbb Z$ this is in general a proper central cut of the whole degree-$d$
algebra $H_d(m)$, and no equality with $H_d(m)$ is asserted. The **tower** is

$$H^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha .$$

It is a unital algebra when $I$ is finite and a locally unital algebra in
general; the ambient tower inclusion is the degree-raising embedding
$\iota\colon H_d(m)\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}(m)$ of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
At level $0$ the tower is concentrated in degree $0$: $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$
and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$.

**(3) Grothendieck groups and the Cartan pairing.** For each $\alpha$ let
$D(A)$ range over representatives of the simple finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules and $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ over their
projective covers. The **module Grothendieck group** $G_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is
the Grothendieck group $G_0$ of the category of finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]])
and the **split projective group** $K_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]); both are taken block
by block and then summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. The **Cartan pairing**

$$\langle-,-\rangle\colon K_0(H^\Lambda)\times G_0(H^\Lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \langle[P],[M]\rangle:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{H^\Lambda}(P,M),$$

is the object-level Hom pairing of
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]; its biadditivity
on the two groups is the descent proved in
[[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]], which also shows
that $\{[Y(A)]\}$ and $\{[D(A)]\}$ are dual bases (over $\mathbb C$ every simple
endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$). Different blocks are orthogonal.

**(4) Residue maps and residue functors.** For $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q^+$
the embedding $\iota$ composed with the projection onto the block
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is the non-unital algebra homomorphism

$$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad u_{\alpha,i}:=\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}(e_\alpha)=\sum_{i\in I_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\ i_{d+1}=i}e(i).$$

The **residue restriction functor** $e_i$ sends a finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$-module $M$ to the vector space
$u_{\alpha,i}M$ viewed as an $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module through
$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$, and the **residue induction functor** $f_i$ sends a
finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module $M$ to
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}M$. Their
well-definedness, exactness, biadjointness, compatibility with the duality
$\circledast$ of (5), and their effect on Grothendieck groups (adjoint operators
for the Cartan pairing, by
[[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]]) are the
content of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]];
summing over $\alpha$ gives endofunctors $e_i,f_i$ of the tower.

**(5) Duality.** The anti-automorphism $\ast$ of $H_d(m)$ with
$s_r^\ast=s_r$ and $x_r^\ast=x_r$ preserves each $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. On
finite-dimensional left $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules put
$M^{\circledast}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(M,\mathbb C)$ with left action
$(hf)(m):=f(m)h^\ast$. This duality fixes every simple module and commutes with
the residue functors; it is the ordinary duality recorded in
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]],
and it is used throughout this page in the form $M^{\circledast}$.

**(6) Stable and admissible data.** A charge datum as above is used in the
form of its admissible stable realization of
[[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]];
stable range means at least $d$ Jordan strings of maximal length $l$, and
admissibility means $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$ for the origin $c$.
These hypotheses are only invoked where the corresponding supplier is used;
the definitions (1)-(5) themselves do not assume them.
